authority_model.syntax_acceptance: HOL4 tools/parsing/HOLSourceParser.sml + HOLSourceAST.sml, cross-checked against SML97 source syntax
authority_model.cakeml_exclusion_test: Pinned CakeML grammar, AST, parse-tree conversion, type inference, and dynamic semantics
authority_model.important_note: HOL4 does not bundle a single machine-readable formal semantics for all host-SML behavior. SML97 supplies normative SML semantics, while HOL4's maintained parser/AST supplies the dialect/surface accepted by HOL4 tooling.

included: SML97 core/declaration/module constructs represented by HOL4's source model but absent/restricted/non-equivalent in CakeML
SML static/dynamic semantic rules where CakeML differs
HOL4-specific source-language extensions represented by HOLSourceAST/HOLSourceParser
Moscow-ML primitive declaration extensions represented by HOL4's source model
excluded: CakeML-equivalent features such as case, if, raise, handle, tuples, lists, andalso, orelse, before
Basis-library/runtime API gaps such as PolyML.Compiler, threads, sockets, Time, BinIO; these are not language-semantic features
Frequency claims: parser-supported features are included even if rare in checked-in HOL4 code

hol4_ast.scope: AST for Standard ML plus HOL-specific source extensions

hol4_parser.scope: Lexer/parser, fixity environment, HOL source forms

hol4_parser_grammar.scope: SML grammar used by HOL4 help/source tooling

cakeml_conversion.scope: Parse tree to CakeML AST conversion

cakeml_howto.freshness_note: Its claim that CakeML lacks open/signatures is stale relative to the pinned grammar; use source grammar/conversion as the authority.

features.name: Record types
features.semantics: Record types carry labeled fields; field order is not the semantic identity of the record type.

cakeml.reason: No record type production in Type grammar and no record constructor in ast_t.

features.name: Record expressions
features.semantics: Record expressions construct labeled products whose components are selected by labels.

cakeml.reason: No record expression production and no record expression AST constructor.

features.name: Record patterns
features.semantics: Record patterns destructure labeled fields during pattern matching.

cakeml.reason: No record pattern production and no record pattern AST constructor.

features.name: Flexible record patterns
features.semantics: Flexible record patterns match a known subset of fields while leaving additional fields unconstrained.

syntax.normalized_ebnf: rowpat ::= label '=' pat | label [':' ty] ['as' pat] | '...'

cakeml.reason: No record rows/flexible-row pattern syntax or AST.

features.name: Record shorthand rows
features.semantics: Record row shorthand binds a field label as a variable, with optional layered-pattern/type forms in HOL4's source model.

cakeml.reason: No record-row shorthand because records are absent.

features.name: Record selectors
features.semantics: A selector #label denotes a function that extracts the field named label from a compatible record.

cakeml.reason: No #label selector production or selector AST.

features.name: `while`
features.semantics: while repeatedly evaluates the condition and body for effects until the condition is false, then returns unit.

cakeml.reason: Current expression grammar has no while production.

features.name: Multi-arm `fn`
features.semantics: A multi-arm anonymous function performs ordered pattern matching across all arms for each application.

cakeml.reason: E accepts only fn Pattern => E; no additional | arms.

features.name: Multi-clause same-name `fun`
features.semantics: Multiple clauses of the same function name form one recursive function with ordered pattern matching over clause patterns.

syntax.normalized_ebnf: dec ::= 'fun' fclause ('|' fclause)+; fclause ::= vid atpat+ [':' ty] '=' exp

cakeml.reason: Each FDecl is one equation; and combines mutually-recursive declarations but there is no same-name | clause family.

features.name: SML constructor declaration syntax
features.semantics: In SML, a constructor has zero or one constructor argument; a tuple can be that single argument. CakeML constructor declarations use a list of curried constructor arguments.

cakeml.reason: CakeML Dconstructor uses a list of base argument types rather than SML's optional single 'of ty' constructor argument.

features.name: Constructor values / partial use
features.semantics: An SML unary constructor is also a first-class function value and can be passed without immediate application.

syntax.normalized_ebnf: exp ::= longvid  # constructor identifier may denote a unary constructor function without immediate argument

cakeml.reason: CakeML requires constructors to be fully applied; constructor-as-function use must be eta-expanded.

features.name: Environment-based constructor naming
features.semantics: SML constructor/value status is determined by the static environment, not by capitalization; the same lexical class can acquire constructor status.

syntax.example: constructor status not fixed by capitalization
syntax.normalized_ebnf: identifier-status ::= resolved from static environment (constructor/exception/value), not capitalization

cakeml.reason: CakeML grammar lexically requires constructor names to start uppercase and alpha-numeric variables/functions lowercase.

features.name: Symbolic / `op` constructor forms
features.semantics: SML permits op-qualified and symbolic value/constructor identifiers where the static environment determines identifier status.

syntax.normalized_ebnf: constructor-id ::= ['op'] vid  # vid may be symbolic where permitted by SML lexical/static rules

cakeml.reason: CakeML's constructor grammar is uppercase-name based; general SML environment-classified symbolic/op constructor forms are not equivalent.

features.name: Real literals
features.semantics: Real constants are source literals denoting real values according to SML lexical and dynamic semantics.

cakeml.reason: Eliteral includes IntT/CharT/StringT/WordT/FFIT but not real literals, despite internal Float64 support.

features.name: Word literal patterns
features.semantics: Word constants can occur as constant patterns and participate in pattern matching.

cakeml.reason: CakeML expression literals include WordT, but Pbase pattern literals omit WordT.

features.name: Full layered pattern binder annotation
features.semantics: A layered pattern can bind an identifier, optionally type-constrain that binder, and simultaneously require a nested pattern.

cakeml.reason: Pas is V as Pcons; a type annotation applies to the whole Pattern, not the SML layered binder form [op] vid [:ty] as pat.

features.name: Full declarations inside expression `let`
features.semantics: The declaration sequence inside let is the general Core declaration language, so local datatypes, types, exceptions, local declarations, etc. affect the body scope.

cakeml.reason: Expression-level LetDec permits only val, fun, and open.

features.name: SuccessorML or-pattern AST support
features.semantics: HOL4's source model includes SuccessorML-style or-patterns, where alternatives are a single pattern form.

syntax.normalized_ebnf: pat ::= pat '|' pat ('|' pat)*  # SuccessorML form represented by HOL4 tooling

cakeml.reason: No or-pattern AST or pattern production.

features.name: `val rec`
features.semantics: val rec provides recursive value binding, typically for function-valued expressions, with recursive scope during evaluation/elaboration.

cakeml.reason: No rec keyword/value-recursive val production.

features.name: Simultaneous `val ... and ...`
features.semantics: val ... and ... forms simultaneous bindings whose right-hand sides share the pre-declaration environment rather than seeing earlier sibling bindings.

syntax.normalized_ebnf: dec ::= 'val' tyvarseq? ['rec'] pat '=' exp ('and' ['rec'] pat '=' exp)+

cakeml.reason: val declaration grammar binds one Pattern = E; no val ... and ... group.

features.name: Explicit declaration tyvar sequence
features.semantics: Core value/function declarations may explicitly bind type variables that scope over the declaration.

cakeml.reason: No explicit tyvar sequence on val/fun declarations.

features.name: `type ... and ...`
features.semantics: type bindings joined by and are elaborated as one simultaneous type-binding group.

cakeml.reason: TypeAbbrevDec is a single type binding; no type ... and ... group.

features.name: `datatype ... withtype ...`
features.semantics: withtype adds simultaneous type abbreviations to a datatype binding group and participates in the group's type scope.

cakeml.reason: No withtype production.

features.name: `abstype`
features.semantics: abstype creates datatype representation internally, exposes an abstract type externally, and hides constructors after the body.

cakeml.reason: No abstype production or abstraction AST.

features.name: Datatype replication
features.semantics: datatype replication re-exports an existing datatype and its constructor identities rather than creating fresh constructors.

cakeml.reason: No datatype replication production.

features.name: Exception replication
features.semantics: exception replication binds a new exception identifier to the same exception identity as an existing exception.

cakeml.reason: No exception replication production.

features.name: Grouped exception declarations
features.semantics: Exception bindings may be grouped with and; each new exception binding is generative while replication preserves identity.

cakeml.reason: Exception declaration accepts one Dconstructor; no and-group.

features.name: `infix`
features.semantics: infix changes the fixity environment for subsequent parsing/elaboration, with an optional precedence.

cakeml.reason: No infix declaration; operators are assigned to fixed lexical precedence classes.

features.name: `infixr`
features.semantics: infixr installs right-associative fixity for subsequent parsing/elaboration.

cakeml.reason: No infixr declaration; associativity is fixed by the CakeML grammar.

features.name: `nonfix`
features.semantics: nonfix removes an identifier's infix status for subsequent parsing/elaboration.

cakeml.reason: No nonfix declaration or mutable fixity environment.

features.name: Multiple paths in one `open`
features.semantics: One open declaration may open multiple structure paths in order.

cakeml.reason: open accepts exactly one ModPath per declaration.

features.name: Named signatures
features.semantics: A signature declaration binds a reusable signature identifier to a signature expression.

cakeml.reason: No signature declaration production or signature AST.

features.name: Signature conformance checking
features.semantics: Signature ascription checks that a structure matches a signature and restricts its externally visible interface.

cakeml.reason: No implemented signature-conformance semantics; restricted inline :> syntax is discarded during conversion.

features.name: Transparent ascription
features.semantics: Transparent ascription constrains the visible interface while preserving type identities that can be inferred from the implementation.

cakeml.reason: No transparent ':' structure ascription syntax/semantics.

features.name: Opaque ascription semantics
features.semantics: Opaque ascription seals a structure and generates abstract type identities for hidden type components.

cakeml.reason: Restricted ':> sig ... end' is parsed, but SpecLine/SignatureValue reduce to unit and ptree_Structure drops asc before constructing Dmod.

features.name: Named signature expressions
features.semantics: A named signature expression refers to a previously bound signature identifier.

cakeml.reason: No named signature expression in structure ascription.

features.name: `where type`
features.semantics: where type refines a signature by equating a specified type component with a concrete type.

cakeml.reason: No where type signature refinement.

features.name: `include` specs
features.semantics: include imports the specifications of one or more signatures into the enclosing signature/specification.

cakeml.reason: No include specification.

features.name: `eqtype` specs
features.semantics: eqtype requires a type component to admit equality.

cakeml.reason: No eqtype specification or equality-kind semantics.

features.name: `sharing type`
features.semantics: sharing type imposes equality/unification constraints between type components.

cakeml.reason: No sharing type specification.

features.name: Structure sharing
features.semantics: Structure sharing constrains named structure components to denote the same compatible structure identity/interface as required by SML module semantics.

cakeml.reason: No structure sharing specification.

features.name: Nested structure specs
features.semantics: Signatures can contain nested structure specifications with their own signature constraints.

cakeml.reason: Restricted SpecLine has val/type/exception/datatype only; no nested structure spec.

features.name: Functor declarations
features.semantics: A functor is a module-level function from a structure argument satisfying a specification/signature to a structure result.

cakeml.reason: No functor declaration or functor AST.

features.name: Functor application
features.semantics: Functor application evaluates/elaborates a functor against a structure expression or inline structure declarations.

cakeml.reason: No functor application structure expression.

features.name: Functor inline-spec args
features.semantics: Functor parameters can be specified inline as a specification sequence rather than only as a named structure plus signature.

cakeml.reason: No functor parameter specification language.

features.name: Structure aliases
features.semantics: A structure expression may simply be a path to an existing structure, enabling structure aliases.

cakeml.reason: Structure source form is only structure Name [restricted :> inline sig] = struct Decls end; no structure-path RHS alias.

features.name: General structure constraints
features.semantics: Structure expressions can themselves be constrained by transparent or opaque signature ascription.

cakeml.reason: No general structure-expression constraints.

features.name: Structure `let` expressions
features.semantics: A structure expression can contain local structure declarations via let ... in ... end.

cakeml.reason: No general structure-expression language and no structure let expression.

features.name: Simultaneous structure bindings
features.semantics: Structure bindings joined by and are one declaration group with SML module scoping rules.

cakeml.reason: No structure ... and ... binding group.

features.name: Rich local/open/include/spec combinations in signatures
features.semantics: The SML module specification language composes declarations such as include, sharing, nested structures, and type/value/exception specifications; CakeML's parsed inline signature fragment is much smaller and is discarded.

syntax.normalized_ebnf: sigexp ::= 'sig' spec* 'end'; spec composes val/type/eqtype/datatype/exception/structure/include/sharing/local/open/fixity forms as permitted by SML

cakeml.reason: No full SML specification language; the small inline signature fragment is semantically discarded.

features.name: Non-top-level let-polymorphism
features.semantics: SML generalizes eligible local value bindings, allowing one let-bound value to be instantiated at multiple types in the body.

syntax.normalized_ebnf: let val x = value in ...x at multiple instantiations... end

ast_or_parser_symbols: SML97 static semantics for value declarations

cakeml.reason: infer_e deliberately disables generalization for non-top-level Let and Letrec.

features.name: Equality type variables
features.semantics: Equality type variables (written with a doubled quote, e.g. ''a) range only over types that admit equality.

cakeml.reason: CakeML has no equality types/equality-kind restriction.

features.name: Equality type specs
features.semantics: Equality-type specifications propagate the requirement that an abstract type admit equality.

cakeml.reason: No eqtype spec or equality-kind propagation.

features.name: SML function-equality rejection
features.semantics: SML's static semantics rejects equality on function types because functions do not admit equality.

syntax.normalized_ebnf: exp ::= exp '=' exp  # rejected statically when operand type does not admit equality

cakeml.reason: Equality inference only constrains the two operand types to be equal; it does not require an equality type.

features.name: SML equality runtime semantics
features.semantics: SML equality is defined only for equality types; function closures are not equality-comparable. CakeML instead makes closure comparisons succeed and treats all closures as equal.

syntax.normalized_ebnf: exp ::= exp '=' exp  # dynamic equality defined only after SML equality-type admissibility

cakeml.reason: do_eq explicitly returns true for any Closure/Recclosure pair.

features.name: SML observable evaluation order
features.semantics: SML specifies an observable evaluation order for expressions; CakeML deliberately uses right-to-left evaluation, so effectful programs can differ.

syntax.normalized_ebnf: application/tuple/record/other effectful expression forms follow SML evaluation order

cakeml.reason: CakeML documents and defines right-to-left evaluation, unlike SML's observable evaluation order.

features.name: `Match` exception
features.semantics: Failure of a case or anonymous-function match raises the predefined Match exception in SML.

syntax.normalized_ebnf: case exp of pat => exp | ...  # no matching arm => raise Match

cakeml.reason: CakeML has no distinct Match exception; source docs state Bind is raised instead.

features.name: `Bind`/`Match` distinction
features.semantics: SML distinguishes Bind (failed value binding) from Match (failed case/function match); CakeML collapses match failure to Bind.

syntax.normalized_ebnf: val pat = exp  # failed binding => Bind; case/fn match failure => Match

cakeml.reason: The SML Bind/Match failure distinction is not preserved.

features.name: Type variables in expression/pattern annotations
features.semantics: SML permits type variables in explicit expression/pattern type annotations when they are correctly scoped; CakeML's AST represents them but its inference rejects them in source annotations.

syntax.normalized_ebnf: exp ::= exp ':' ty; pat ::= pat ':' ty; ty may contain scoped type variables

cakeml.reason: Atvar exists in the AST, but inference reports that type variables are not supported in source type annotations.

features.name: Dynamic fixity environment
features.semantics: Fixity declarations mutate a scoped fixity environment that determines how later infix source text is parsed; CakeML instead uses fixed operator classes.

cakeml.reason: No scoped user-defined fixity environment; grammar fixes precedence classes by operator spelling.

features.name: Opaque type identity/sealing
features.semantics: Opaque sealing creates fresh abstract type identity and prevents clients from relying on hidden representation equalities.

cakeml.reason: No implemented opaque sealing/fresh abstract type identity; parsed restricted :> data is dropped.

features.name: `abstype` representation hiding
features.semantics: abstype representation hiding makes constructors available only inside the with ... end body and exposes only the abstract type outside.

cakeml.reason: No abstype declaration or representation-hiding semantics.

features.name: Theory header language
features.semantics: HOL4 theory headers declare the theory name and source-level Ancestors/Libs metadata consumed by HOL tooling.

cakeml.reason: No HOL4 Theory/Ancestors/Libs source declaration in CakeML.

features.name: Definition blocks
features.semantics: Definition blocks package quoted HOL terms plus optional termination proof/tactic material into a source declaration.

cakeml.reason: No HOL Definition block syntax.

features.name: Theorem blocks
features.semantics: Theorem blocks package a theorem statement quotation and proof/tactic body, terminated by QED; HOL4 also supports simple theorem-binding forms.

cakeml.reason: No HOL Theorem/Proof/QED declaration syntax.

features.name: `Triviality`
features.semantics: Triviality is a theorem-declaration variant with different registration/export intent in HOL tooling.

cakeml.reason: No HOL Triviality declaration syntax.

features.name: `Inductive` / `CoInductive`
features.semantics: Inductive and CoInductive blocks introduce rule systems from quoted HOL syntax and invoke HOL-specific elaboration.

cakeml.reason: No HOL Inductive/CoInductive declaration syntax.

features.name: HOL `Datatype:` command
features.semantics: HOL4's Datatype: ... End command is a quotation-based HOL datatype declaration distinct from SML datatype.

cakeml.reason: No HOL Datatype: ... End command syntax.

features.name: HOL quotations
features.semantics: HOL quotations embed HOL term/type concrete syntax inside SML/HOL source.

syntax.normalized_ebnf: HOL quotation delimiters / full-quote forms containing quoted HOL source

cakeml.reason: No HOL quotation syntax/AST.

features.name: Antiquotation
features.semantics: Antiquotation splices an SML expression into a HOL quotation.

cakeml.reason: No HOL antiquotation syntax/AST.

features.name: `Quote` declarations
features.semantics: Quote declarations bind named quotation material for user-supplied parsing/elaboration.

cakeml.reason: No HOL Quote declaration syntax.

features.name: HOL `Type` / `Overload` declarations
features.semantics: HOL Type and Overload declarations modify HOL's logical type/overload environment from source.

cakeml.reason: No HOL logical Type/Overload declaration syntax.

features.name: `Resume` / `Finalise`
features.semantics: Resume and Finalise are HOL proof-workflow declarations for suspended/finalized theorem construction.

cakeml.reason: No HOL Resume/Finalise declarations.

features.name: HOL attributes
features.semantics: HOL declarations accept attribute lists that control theorem/definition processing and metadata.

cakeml.reason: No HOL declaration attribute syntax/semantics.

features.name: `#(LINE)` / `#(FILE)` pragmas
features.semantics: HOL #(LINE) and #(FILE) pragmas alter source-location mapping used by tooling and diagnostics.

cakeml.reason: No HOL #(LINE)/#(FILE) pragmas.

features.name: Moscow ML `prim_val`
features.semantics: Moscow ML prim_val binds an SML identifier directly to a runtime primitive described by arity/name metadata.

syntax.normalized_ebnf: dec ::= 'prim_val' tyvarseq id [':' ty] ['=' arity primitive-name] ('and' ...)*

cakeml.reason: No Moscow ML prim_val syntax.

features.name: Moscow ML `prim_type`
features.semantics: Moscow ML prim_type introduces a primitive type constructor supplied by the implementation.

cakeml.reason: No Moscow ML prim_type syntax.

features.name: Moscow ML `prim_eqtype`
features.semantics: Moscow ML prim_eqtype introduces an implementation primitive type that admits equality.

cakeml.reason: No Moscow ML prim_eqtype syntax.

features.name: Moscow ML `prim_EQtype`
features.semantics: Moscow ML prim_EQtype introduces the implementation's stronger primitive reference/equality-type form.

cakeml.reason: No Moscow ML prim_EQtype syntax.
